title: Sally S NDE 7460
content: I had undergone surgery to remove my tonsils and adenoids. After returning home, I began hemorrhaging, and returned to the hospital for treatment. I experienced this twice, and upon my second visit to the hospital, a blood clot formed preventing me from breathing. That night I remember being in pain. I felt very frightened, but suddenly I no longer felt the pain. This wonderful sensation of peace flowed through me, and I floated out of my body. I was in a pediatric ward with two other girls and I remember looking down on each of them as they slept. Suddenly, a beautiful voice told me that it was not my time, that I had more to do and that I would marry and have a boy and a girl. I was also told that my life would not be easy, but I would never be alone. As I continued to look around from above, I saw a nurse come into the ward. She checked the two girls and when she came to stand beside me, she suddenly ran out of the room. I saw her return with other people who gathered around me. They began pushing my crib type bed out of the room and down the hallway. A long hose was placed down my throat and suddenly I returned to my body. Later that same year I began to experience Petit-Mal seizures that continued until the age of 17. I began for some reason to look for someone named Steve Smith, whom I later married in 1974. I had a boy in 1976 and a girl in 1980. In 1997, my husband was diagnosed with Carcinoid Syndrome, and later died in 2002 after retiring from the U.S. Navy Reserves after 26 years. He had been an Architect for many years in his family business.

boundary_and_return.mission_detail: Told she 'had more to do' and would marry and have a boy and a girl; life would not be easy but she would never be alone.

stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: Peace/pain cessation and OBE in hospital ward with guidance ('not my time'), then return during medical intervention; no tunnel/light/life review described.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Prophetic statements about future spouse and children; later searched for a person by the name given ('Steve Smith') and later married him; later health issues (Petit-Mal seizures) mentioned after the event.
